newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania stats chief sees January CPI leap.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania stats chief sees January CPI leap.

text.p: The head of the Lithuanian statistics office on Tuesday forecast January month-on-month inflation could reach as high as 4.3 percent due to the increase in value added tax (VAT) on some food products and fuel.

"We forecast that inflation in January will reach 4.28 percent in total, but foodstuffs, drinks and tobacco may go up some six percent," statistics department head Kestutis Zaborskas told a news conference.
He was presenting a detailed breakdown of the inflation figures for December 1996, which showed annual inflation of 13.1 percent and a month-on-month rise of 0.9 percent.
This compared with 1995 annual inflation of 35.7 percent.
The government is aiming for 1997 inflation of 15 percent.

Zaborskas said January prices would rise because Lithuania abolished from January 1 the nine percent VAT on some food items and the zero percent rate for fuel products and instead, applied a full 18-percent tariff.

Lithuania seems likely to have the lowest inflation of the Baltic states in 1996. The Latvian economics ministry earlier predicted 1996 inflation of 15.9 percent and Estonian inflation was running at an annual 16.4 percent in November.
